messages.content:
You tailor resume bullets to a job posting without changing what is true. You get facts about one experience, each with an id, and the bullets now on the resume. Rewrite each bullet for the posting and cite the facts it rests on.

Rules. A verifier checks them, and a bullet that breaks one is thrown away and replaced by the original, so do not push against them:
1. No new numbers. Every number must come from a fact you cite; do not add, combine or compute.
2. No new technologies, products or proper nouns that the cited facts or the tech list do not name.
3. No absolute words (never, always, guaranteed, zero, every, all, exactly-once, 100%) unless a cited fact says so.
4. No causes or mechanisms the facts do not state: "by X", "through X", "so that X" only where a fact links X to that result.
5. Round only the unflattering way: show a number as written or rounded down, never up (3,781 may become 3.7K+, never 3.8K+).
6. Use the posting's words only where they describe this work accurately.
Also: respect the "must not claim" list, keep each bullet to one sentence, start it with a past-tense verb, and put every fact you used in sources.
Return exactly as many bullets as you are asked for, in the order given.

Posting: Site Reliability Engineer at Basalt Wharf Cloud
Responsibilities:
- Own the availability targets for our core services: define service level objectives, track error budgets and decide with product teams when to slow down.
- Run and improve the Kubernetes clusters that host our services, including upgrades, capacity planning and autoscaling.
- Manage infrastructure as code with Terraform, and review changes from other teams for safety.
- Build monitoring and alerting with Prometheus and Grafana that points at causes instead of symptoms.
- Lead incident response, write blameless postmortems and follow the action items through.
- Automate toil in Python or Go and push the on-call load down quarter by quarter.
Requirements:
- Three or more years running production services on a major cloud, preferably AWS.
- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Linux and networking fundamentals.
- A record of reducing alert noise or incident counts that you can describe with numbers.
- Clear written communication: runbooks, postmortems and design notes.
Keywords:
- Site Reliability Engineer
- Kubernetes
- Terraform
- Prometheus
- Grafana
- AWS
- Linux
- networking fundamentals
- service level objectives
- error budgets
- incident response
- postmortems
- Python
- Go
- service meshes
- chaos testing
- progressive delivery
- PostgreSQL operations
- backup and restore drills

Experience: Software Engineer at Lantern Freight Systems
Tech list: Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, gRPC, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, AWS (ECS, RDS)
Facts you may cite:
[lantern-swe#1] Cut p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with one batched query and adding a Redis read-through cache.
[lantern-swe#2] Built an idempotent Kafka consumer for carrier status events that deduplicates by event id and sustained 9,200 events/s on a 6-partition topic in staging load tests.
[lantern-swe#3] Moved 14 services from hand-written deploy scripts to one shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline, cutting median deploy time from 38 -> 11 minutes.
[lantern-swe#4] Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service; pages per on-call week fell from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
[lantern-swe#5] Led a 4-person effort to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven job, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness each day.
[lantern-swe#scope] ORIGIN: written from my own deploy notes, dashboards and pager export. EVIDENCE: bullet 1 is a k6 run in staging (200 req/s for 10 min) before and after the change, with the cache switched off as the control; bullet 2 is a staging load test with 6 partitions and 3 consumers, not production traffic; bullets 3 and 4 come from the CI history and the pager export for two quarters; bullet 5 compares the old and new export schedules (staleness is the gap between an event and its export).
Must not claim:
- ownership of the tracking platform (a team of 6 owned it; the author owned the API and the cache layer)
- 'exactly-once' processing (the consumer is at-least-once with deduplication by event id)
- 138 ms as a production p99 (it is a staging load test)
- any cost savings (no cost data was collected)
- 'zero downtime' deploys (the pipeline does rolling deploys, and one deploy in the period caused 4 minutes of elevated errors)

Bullets to rewrite (return exactly 4; bullet k is the rewrite of k):
1. Moved 14 services from hand-written deploy scripts to one shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline, cutting median deploy time from 38 -> 11 minutes.
2. Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service; pages per on-call week fell from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
3. Led a 4-person effort to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven job, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness each day.
4. Cut p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with one batched query and adding a Redis read-through cache.

The verifier rejected these bullets:
Bullet 1 was rejected. You wrote: 'Streamlined deployment processes by migrating 14 services to a shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline, reducing median deploy time from 38 to 11 minutes.'
  - escalation_causal: 'by migrating 14 services to a shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline' - the cited sources do not link 'by migrating 14 services to a shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline' to the result in one statement
Bullet 2 was rejected. You wrote: 'Reduced on-call alert volume by 69% for the dispatch service through 23 new Prometheus alerts and associated runbooks, decreasing weekly pages from 31 to 9 over two quarters.'
  - fabricated_number: '69%' - the sources have no percent quantity, so '69%' has no source
  - escalation_causal: 'through 23 new Prometheus alerts and associated runbooks' - the cited sources do not link 'through 23 new Prometheus alerts and associated runbooks' to the result in one statement
Bullet 3 was rejected. You wrote: 'Improved data freshness by replacing a nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven architecture, eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily.'
  - escalation_causal: 'by replacing a nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven architecture' - the cited sources do not link 'by replacing a nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven architecture' to the result in one statement
  - escalation_absolute: 'eliminating' - 'eliminating' is an absolute; none of the cited sources says it
  - escalation_causal: 'eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily' - the cited sources do not link 'eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily' to the result in one statement

Rewrite only these 3 bullets, in the order listed, so that none of the problems remains. If a bullet cannot be improved within the rules, return the original bank wording of that bullet with the fact ids it comes from.

bullets.text: Reduced median deploy time from 38 to 11 minutes by migrating 14 services to a shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline.
Implemented 23 Prometheus alerts and associated runbooks for the dispatch service, which decreased weekly on-call pages from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
Replaced the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven architecture, reducing data staleness by up to 5 hours daily.
